goal: Lock Bora's standing discovery preferences so every fresh Career OS chat prioritizes employer-posted roles in explicit one/two/three-week pursuit windows and actively favors remote, contract/contract-to-hire/temporary, and part-time work arrangements, while preserving all existing Candidate Truth, Match Truth, Qualification Truth, authorization, first-party actionability, and package gates.
acceptance_conditions: reliable employer posting age 0-7 days is the GOLD_WINDOW and should be searched/surfaced first by default
reliable employer posting age 8-14 days is the STRETCH_WINDOW; 15-21 days is the FAR_STRETCH_WINDOW; 22+ days is EXCEPTION_ONLY_WINDOW unless unusually strong and first-party verified live/actionable

the existing Freshness vocabulary VERY_FRESH/FRESH/AGING/STALE_LEANING/UNKNOWN remains unchanged and the new pursuit-window labels are governance/presentation vocabulary only, not schema or runtime enum values

REMOTE, CONTRACT/CONTRACT-TO-HIRE/TEMPORARY, and PART_TIME are explicit positive discovery preferences; combinations such as remote plus contract or remote plus part-time receive strong tiebreak priority among otherwise comparable opportunities

work-format and recency preferences never rescue weak fit, change qualification, override authorization blockers, bypass first-party actionability, or suppress an unusually strong otherwise-accessible role
where employer posting date is unavailable or unreliable, preserve UNKNOWN and never substitute discovered_date/date_first_seen as employer posting date
fresh chats receive the rule through the always-on .cursor/rules/role-selection.mdc pointer without requiring Bora to repeat the preference
no runtime product code, schema, Candidate Truth, Match Truth, qualification, immigration/authorization, first-party actionability, resume/package doctrine, or pinned Blueprint v3.13 banner changes
stop_conditions: implementation requires any path outside allowed_paths
implementation would create numeric scoring, a persisted freshness/work-format enum, or a hard filter that changes Qualification Truth
implementation would weaken authorization, first-party actionability, Candidate/Match Truth, or package-gate controls
independent review finds a material ambiguity or contradiction with existing Section 138 doctrine
